sources.title: Phase transitions for the existence of unregularized M-estimators in single index models
inspected_units: Section 3 relation to the nonlinear-system problem
sources.version_note: The accessible arXiv v2 uses Assumption 2 and Theorem 2.4. Numbering is explicit in the revised manuscript; it is not silently attributed to the publication PDF.
sources.established: Gaussian single-index existence threshold for the stated rowwise convex losses. The expected absolute rowwise infimum is finite.
sources.mathematical_difference: A labelled compensated row has strictly negative recession in the realized human separation direction and infimum minus infinity. For an exterior design the entire objective is unbounded below; positive scaling and finite constants preserve this property. A finite sum of finite-infimum row losses is bounded below, so it cannot be an identical objective on such designs.
sources.contribution_scope: The two-sample compensation boundary requires an argument for this specified loss class. The stated general theorem is not directly applicable. This observation does not exclude a different dual/event-level reduction or claim new conic machinery.
sources.current_reading_limit: The publisher-linked PDF is listed in the official mlresearch/v267 repository, blob df90a43aea28151020bff1e7906c8c95c097ec1f, 1592652 bytes. Web rejected its content type and the GitHub connector cannot decode that PDF; no current PDF theorem reading is claimed.

sources.title: Covariance-Calibrated Prediction-Powered Inference
sources.established: Complete GMM, covariance calibration, and first-order-equivalent estimators with different finite-sample fits or risks are established.
sources.mathematical_difference: The present probability boundary is for the scalar compensated convex loss. The same-design B6 comparison proves finite complete-GMM attainment while that loss is unbounded. The oracle score path holds its realized truth score and full oracle covariance fixed within the scalar family.
sources.contribution_scope: No generic first-order/finite-sample novelty, new calibration method, or risk ordering against complete GMM is claimed. The exact proportional-dimensional boundary and its same-objective consequences carry the candidate contribution.

sources.title: The generalization error of max-margin linear classifiers
sources.established: A strictly positive limiting human separation margin in the isotropic model above its ordinary threshold.
sources.mathematical_difference: Proposition 6 combines this existing margin theorem with the same compensated objective finite-root event and an explicit gradient-aware finite-design inequality. It concludes new-row proper-loss divergence for its vanishing positive powers.
sources.contribution_scope: A consequence of the paper boundary, not an independent new maximum-margin theorem. The negative result supplies the cost of maximizing availability.

sources.title: Boosting as a Regularized Path to a Maximum Margin Classifier
sources.established: Generic weak-regularization margin paths and diverging coefficients are established.
sources.mathematical_difference: Appendix D uses the actual corrected auxiliary recession cost, which may be negative away from the human separation cone. Its specified positive condition, existence envelope and finite-design error terms are retained.
sources.contribution_scope: Generic coefficient blow-up and margin selection are not separate innovation claims.

sources.title: On the existence of maximum likelihood estimators in a multinomial choice model under positivity constraints
sources.established: The stated subject is a positivity-constrained multinomial likelihood and an additional monotonicity requirement.
sources.mathematical_difference: The current parameter domain is unrestricted and the loss contains labelled subtraction. The paper distinguishes a finite-design support criterion from the explicit two-sample Gaussian probability boundary.
sources.contribution_scope: General multinomial existence criteria and interior/boundary distinctions remain established. Full theorem-equivalence exclusion is not claimed from an abstract.
